sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff, §§9.2 and 12.3; North Star scope
sol.problem: The proposal changes certificate layout and root identity without stating how a mixed fat object uses them. Neither the note nor INDEX's shared publication decisions identifies the embedded device object as the binding subject or explains certificate inventory alongside native host code. This fails the council's explicit standing mixed-fat-object check, independently of the otherwise sound applicability repair.
sol.fix: Append to §12.3: 'A mixed fat object may contain native host code together with embedded ISA objects and certificates for their oracle or action roots. Each certificate's object_hash binds its embedded ISA object; interface_hash, closure_hash and reference_program_hash identify the selected device root under §9.2. The fat-object container associates each certificate with that embedded object and root closure, and a composed certificate retains linked device proof records under their owner closure hashes. Native host code outside the tainted call graph remains native and is not required to appear as ISA regions or carry oracle comparison claims or fault censuses.' This permits a container inventory or separate per-root packets; I would use separate per-root packets associated by object and root closure hashes.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff — §§9.2 and 12.3; Defect and North Star scope
codex.problem: The proposal changes certificate root identity and linked owner-record inventory but provides no mixed-fat-object application statement. INDEX's general no-narrowing assertion does not identify which embedded object/root these bindings name or explain that native-only code remains outside the region inventory. This fails the explicitly required bennett-4ht standing check against North Star §§2, 3.3 and 4.4.
codex.fix: Append to §12.3, cross-referenced from §9.2: 'For a mixed fat object, these certificate bindings apply to each embedded or linked ISA object and its certified device-region root. object_hash identifies that ISA object; reference_program_hash identifies the interface of the oracle or action root selected by bindings.closure_hash. Neither field identifies the native host binary or its entry point. The fat-object certificate inventory may aggregate certificates for multiple device roots. Each composed regions map contains the relevant device-region owner records and checked linked-library proofs; native-only code requires no region record, oracle comparison, fault census or inverse-pair entry. These rules do not require lifting the native host or unmarked code.' Example: native main with marked device roots A and B carries certificates rooted at A and B, with their respective ISA-object bindings; main is not a required regions entry. No container encoding or launch implementation is required by this clarification.
